correctness.rationale: On the complete Fourier basis, the squared Hilbert–Schmidt commutator is exactly 2 Theta_(2I) minus 2 Theta_(I+A^T A). Poisson summation gives the exact infinite-lattice expansion because both Gaussian quadratic forms are positive. The determinant is ||A||_F^2+2 for each unimodular A. For the two concrete matrices the inverse form has shortest nonzero squared length 1/10 and 1/5 with multiplicity two; next distinct values are 2/5 and 3/10. Their nonzero exponential coefficients give the stated uniform remainder after standard Gaussian tail estimates. Since cost at most 18 bounds all integer entries by 4, a complete integer enumeration lists every hyperbolic matrix in the range and produces explicit GL(2,Z) equivalence witnesses within each lower-cost fixed-trace class. The standalone exact checker passed. Numerical examples are not used to prove the infinite expansion.

value.rationale: The exact least Euclidean complexity of two entropy- and matrix-singular-spectrum-matched hyperbolic dynamics that spatial Gaussian smoothing can distinguish is a natural rigidity boundary. The nonzero separation lies beyond every polynomial-order heat expansion and quantifies precisely why dynamical eigenvalues plus Euclidean singular values cannot recover an arithmetic operator-ideal response. The lower-cost classification is complete, and the cost-18 witness is not an arbitrary slice or a minor improved constant. This is a specific spectral-geometric invariant, not a claim of a general new theta theorem.
